name: Winter Showcase (Winter Formal)
dances: Solo, trio, PITCH groups, class dances
notes: First performance of the season. Must be back for rehearsals Sat Jan 2. Participation fee TBA. Treat it as the dress rehearsal for the January comps.
fun: Season kickoff! Everyone at Glass House performs, and it's the first time the solo, trio and PITCH dances are seen by an audience. Rehearsal Sat Jan 2 is a must.

name: Press Play Seattle
dances: Convention classes only — using the $200 voucher
notes: No Pitch competing. Tiring weekend between two performances: hydrate, eat, sleep, no solo practice. Priority is studio rehearsals for Hollywood Connection the next week.
fun: Press Play was started in 2025 by famous convention directors, and the teachers are big names — Mandy Moore choreographed Taylor Swift's Eras Tour and La La Land, Ricky Ubeda won So You Think You Can Dance. There's a dance-off called The Pop-Off at lunch and a closing show called The Rewind. Family at home can watch the competition on a free livestream.

name: Hollywood Connection
venue: Hyatt Regency Lake Washington, 1053 Lake Washington Blvd N, Renton (venue = hotel)
notes: First real competition. After the Showcase, fix at most two things. No new corrections after Jan 19.
cost: Convention $384 (7+) · Comp: solo $180, trio $110 pp, groups $96 pp
fun: The venue IS the hotel, right on Lake Washington in Renton. Founded by a real Hollywood talent agent, so scholarships can include agency exposure. Sunday ends with a Wrap Party where awards and scholarships are announced. Ballrooms are cold — bring the team jacket. Free class recaps show up on Vimeo afterward.

name: Mid-winter break (school)
notes: Ryze falls at the end of this week.

name: Ryze Seattle
notes: Must be available for rehearsals Thursday Feb 18.
cost: Convention $420 (mini–senior) · Comp: solo $245, trio $125 pp, groups $98 pp
fun: Brand new this year — Seattle is only about its 10th event ever! Started by Randi and Hef, a hip-hop duo who danced for Beyoncé, Janet Jackson and J.Lo. There's a surprise class every Friday night called the SurpRYZE class, a RYZE & Shine warm-up on Saturday, and a Pop-Off jam. Fewer dancers in year one means better scholarship odds.

name: iD Competition
venue: Greater Tacoma Convention Center, 1500 Commerce St, Tacoma
hotel: Marriott Tacoma Downtown is across the street
notes: Back-to-back weekend after Ryze. Watch her energy.
cost: Comp: solo $215, trio $108 pp · $20 media fee per dancer
fun: iD's first-ever stop in Washington. It's a concert-style show: LED backdrop, an MC who talks to the crowd, and a buzzer moment called the ICON Award. It's loud — little siblings may want ear protection. All photos and videos of every routine are included, so no extra media to buy. Free livestream for family.

name: Gravit8 Seattle
venue: Expected Greater Tacoma Convention Center (2027 venue TBD)
cost: Comp: solo $198, trio $96 pp, groups $85 pp
fun: The free-everything comp: free to watch, free photos AND videos of every dancer, free livestream, free T-shirt and neck medals. Judges record spoken critiques you can listen to afterward. There's a $10 Cre8 improv challenge for a little extra stage time. Schedule only shows up on the G8 app the week of the event.

name: Hollywood Vibe Seattle
dances: PITCH groups · solo/trio TBA depending on event caps
cost: Convention $410 (7+) · Comp: solo $250, trio $125 pp, groups $96 pp
fun: Founded in 1998, so lots of history. Teachers have included Liz Imperio (Madonna and J.Lo tours), Kent Boyd and Alexa Anderson from So You Think You Can Dance, and Sasha Farber from Dancing with the Stars. Top winners can earn a trip to LA to train at Millennium Dance Complex. Sunday ends with a faculty show where the teachers perform. Saturday comp can run past midnight!

name: Showstopper Tacoma
venue: Greater Tacoma Convention Center, 1500 Commerce St, Tacoma
cost: Comp: solo $255, trio $128 pp, groups $96 pp
fun: America's oldest dance competition — started in 1978 and used to be on TV. Huge: 1,000+ routines in a weekend, 18 style categories, and every dancer gets an award. Free to watch (bring grandparents) and every routine is livestreamed. Top soloists can get an All-Star invite to the Finals at the Disneyland Hotel in July.

name: 2027–28 Team Auditions
fun: Camp Apex: Minis audition day one, older teams days two and three. It's where next season's teams get set.

name: Glass House Ball 11
fun: Festival-style year-end show at Lake Sammamish State Park — outdoors, free, no tickets, food trucks, and every single dancer performs.
